017package org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter;
018
019import static org.apache.juneau.commons.utils.Shorts.*;
020
021import java.io.*;
022import java.nio.charset.*;
023import java.util.function.*;
024
025import org.apache.juneau.rest.server.*;
026
027import jakarta.servlet.*;
028import jakarta.servlet.http.*;
029
030/**
031 * Applies a {@link RequestBoundary} to every request reaching the servlet container, rejecting those that did not
032 * come from a page this application served.
033 *
034 * <h5 class='section'>Why a servlet filter, and not a mixin or a guard</h5>
035 * <p>
036 * The boundary's value depends entirely on there being no way around it, and the two lighter-weight Juneau
037 * mechanisms both leave one:
038 * <ul>
039 *    <li>A {@link org.apache.juneau.rest.server.guard.RestGuard RestGuard} is declared per resource or per operation, so
040 *       an endpoint added later is unprotected until someone remembers to declare it &mdash; and its omission is
041 *       invisible in review, because nothing about the new endpoint looks different.
042 *    <li>A mixin's {@link RestStartCall @RestStartCall} hook fires only for requests
043 *       that resolved to one of that mixin's own endpoints, so a boundary packaged that way would not see the host
044 *       resource's operations at all.
045 * </ul>
046 * <p>
047 * A filter registered at {@code /*} sees every request the container handles: every Juneau resource and mixin,
048 * static resources served by the container or by another framework in the same application, and the paths that
049 * resolve to nothing and would 404.  Nothing can opt out by omission, which is the property that makes it worth
050 * having.
051 *
052 * <h5 class='section'>Rejection behavior</h5>
053 * <p>
054 * A rejected request is answered directly and the chain is not invoked, so the request never reaches application
055 * code.  The response carries the boundary's chosen status, a {@value #REJECTION_HEADER} header naming the
056 * {@link BoundaryReason reason}, {@code Cache-Control: no-store}, and a small JSON body carrying the same reason and a
057 * message.
058 * <p>
059 * A rejection is never rendered as an empty result or a silent no-op.  A security refusal that looks like "no data"
060 * teaches the user to ignore it, and the point of answering explicitly is that a genuine misconfiguration &mdash;
061 * the application being reached at {@code localhost} when it accepts {@code 127.0.0.1}, say &mdash; is immediately
062 * diagnosable instead of presenting as an inexplicably broken page.
063 *
064 * <h5 class='section'>Token availability to the page renderer</h5>
065 * <p>
066 * On an allowed request the boundary's {@link RequestBoundary#tokenFor(HttpServletRequest) token for that request}
067 * is placed under the {@link #TOKEN_ATTRIBUTE} request attribute, and the header name it must be sent back under is
068 * placed under the {@link #HEADER_ATTRIBUTE} sibling attribute, so a page-rendering endpoint can embed both without
069 * needing its own reference to the boundary.
070 * <p>
071 * A page that embeds the token in more than one place should give each place its own value: a {@link CsrfBoundary}
072 * masks its token under a fresh pad on every call, so the secret never repeats in the page.  For that the filter also
073 * places a {@code Supplier<String>} under {@link #TOKEN_SUPPLIER_ATTRIBUTE}; each {@code get()} returns a new value.
074 * Read it from the servlet request and test it with {@code instanceof TokenSupplier}: converting the attribute to a string
075 * yields the supplier's own description, not a token.  {@link #TOKEN_ATTRIBUTE} keeps a single value for renderers
076 * that read only a string.
077 * <p>
078 * A response that embeds the token must not be cached, or a cache hands the token to whoever asks next.  The code
079 * that writes the token calls {@link #markTokenBearing(HttpServletResponse)} before it writes any of the body; this
080 * filter cannot know which responses embed it.
081 *
082 * <h5 class='section'>Sessions</h5>
083 * <p>
084 * A {@link CsrfBoundary} with a {@linkplain CsrfTokens#perSession() per-session} token needs the session to exist
085 * before the page is written, or the page carries a token that verifies against nothing.  The boundary itself never
086 * creates one; this filter does, with {@link HttpServletRequest#getSession(boolean) getSession(true)}, and only when
087 * all of these hold:
088 * <ul>
089 *    <li>{@link CsrfBoundary#createSessions()} is on (the default);
090 *    <li>the request is allowed and its effective method is safe;
091 *    <li>the request looks like a page load: {@code Sec-Fetch-Mode: navigate} or {@code Sec-Fetch-Dest: document} or
092 *       {@code iframe}; or, with no {@code Sec-Fetch-*} header at all, an {@code Accept} header naming
093 *       {@code text/html}.
094 * </ul>
095 * <p>
096 * So a {@code curl} {@code GET} with {@code Accept: *}{@code /*} never creates a session, while a client that asks
097 * for HTML, Juneau's own HTML REST pages included, does.  The filter never changes a session id and never sets cookie
098 * attributes; those stay the application's (see {@link CsrfBoundary}).
099 *
100 * <h5 class='section'>Registration: order and dispatcher types</h5>
101 * <p>
102 * Map the filter at {@code /*} so nothing can be reached around it.  Register it ahead of any filter that acts on the
103 * request on the application's behalf.  A {@link CsrfBoundary} using
104 * {@link CsrfBoundary.OriginSource#CONTAINER CONTAINER} is the exception that must come <i>after</i> one filter: the
105 * container's forwarded-header rewrite, when that is a filter (Spring Boot's {@code ForwardedHeaderFilter} sits at
106 * {@code Ordered.HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE}, so register this one strictly later).
107 * <p>
108 * The filter judges every request it is handed, whatever its {@link DispatcherType}; it has no dispatch-type check of
109 * its own, so which dispatches it sees is decided entirely by the registration.  Register it for
110 * {@link DispatcherType#REQUEST REQUEST} only unless there is a reason to do otherwise:
111 * <ul>
112 *    <li>an {@code ERROR} dispatch of a refused or failed write may arrive without the token header and be refused in
113 *       turn, replacing the error page with a 403;
114 *    <li>a {@code FORWARD} to an HTML view looks like a page load and can create a session.
115 * </ul>
116 * <p>
117 * {@code ASYNC}, {@code ERROR} and {@code FORWARD} are opt-in.  A container's default registration (a
118 * {@code null} dispatcher set in {@code addMappingForUrlPatterns}, or Spring Boot's {@code FilterRegistrationBean}
119 * default) is {@code REQUEST} only.
120 *
121 * <h5 class='section'>Example (Spring Boot):</h5>
122 * <p class='bjava'>
123 *    <ja>@Bean</ja>
124 *    <jk>public</jk> FilterRegistrationBean&lt;RequestBoundaryFilter&gt; boundary(RequestBoundary <jv>b</jv>) {
125 *       <jk>var</jk> <jv>reg</jv> = <jk>new</jk> FilterRegistrationBean&lt;&gt;(<jk>new</jk> RequestBoundaryFilter(<jv>b</jv>));
126 *       <jv>reg</jv>.addUrlPatterns(<js>"/*"</js>);
127 *       <jv>reg</jv>.setOrder(Ordered.<jsf>HIGHEST_PRECEDENCE</jsf>);
128 *       <jk>return</jk> <jv>reg</jv>;
129 *    }
130 * </p>
131 *
132 * <h5 class='section'>See Also:</h5><ul>
133 *    <li class='jic'>{@link RequestBoundary}
134 *    <li class='jc'>{@link LoopbackBoundaryFilter}
135 * </ul>
136 *
137 * @since 10.0.0
138 */
139public class RequestBoundaryFilter implements Filter {
140
141   /** Request attribute under which an allowed request carries the CSRF token value a page embeds. */
142   public static final String TOKEN_ATTRIBUTE = "org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter.csrfToken";
143
144   /**
145    * Request attribute under which an allowed request carries the boundary's CSRF <b>header name</b>
146    * ({@link RequestBoundary#csrfHeader()}).
147    *
148    * <p>
149    * Published as a sibling of {@link #TOKEN_ATTRIBUTE} on the same allowed-request path so a page-rendering
150    * document shell (e.g. the console {@code <@console>} FTL directive) can emit both the {@code csrf-token} meta
151    * value <b>and</b> the header name the client script must send it back under, without needing its own reference
152    * to the boundary.
153    */
154   public static final String HEADER_ATTRIBUTE = "org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter.csrfHeader";
155
156   /**
157    * Request attribute under which an allowed request carries a {@code Supplier<String>} of CSRF token values, one
158    * per {@code get()}.
159    *
160    * <p>
161    * Each value is {@link RequestBoundary#tokenFor(HttpServletRequest)} called afresh, so a masking boundary gives every
162    * embed in a page its own pad.  Read the attribute from the servlet request and check it with
163    * {@code instanceof TokenSupplier}; never convert it to a string.
164    *
165    * <p>
166    * Request code can call {@code setAttribute} on this name, so a reader must trust the value only when it is a
167    * {@link TokenSupplier}, a type only this filter can create.  A value of any other type under this name was put
168    * there by someone else: treat it as "no token" and fail closed, rather than embed what it returns.
169    */
170   public static final String TOKEN_SUPPLIER_ATTRIBUTE = "org.apache.juneau.rest.server.filter.csrfTokenSupplier";
171
172   /**
173    * The {@code Supplier<String>} this filter publishes under {@link #TOKEN_SUPPLIER_ATTRIBUTE}.
174    *
175    * <p>
176    * It has no public constructor, so request code that overwrites the attribute cannot produce one; a reader that
177    * accepts only this type ignores any replacement.  Each {@link #get()} is the boundary's token for the request
178    * afresh.
179    */
180   public static final class TokenSupplier implements Supplier<String> {
181
182      private final RequestBoundary boundary;
183      private final HttpServletRequest req;
184
185      private TokenSupplier(RequestBoundary boundary, HttpServletRequest req) {
186         this.boundary = boundary;
187         this.req = req;
188      }
189
190      @Override /* Supplier */
191      public String get() {
192         return boundary.tokenFor(req);
193      }
194   }
195
196   /** Response header naming the {@link BoundaryReason} a request was rejected for. */
197   public static final String REJECTION_HEADER = "X-Request-Boundary";
198
199   private final RequestBoundary boundary;
200
201   /**
202    * Constructor.
203    *
204    * @param boundary The boundary to apply to every request.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
205    */
206   public RequestBoundaryFilter(RequestBoundary boundary) {
207      this.boundary = reqnn("boundary", boundary);
208   }
209
210   /**
211    * The boundary this filter applies.
212    *
213    * @return The boundary.
214    */
215   public RequestBoundary boundary() { return boundary; }
216
217   /**
218    * Marks a response that embeds a CSRF token as one no cache may store.
219    *
220    * <p>
221    * Sets {@code Cache-Control: private, no-store}, replacing any value already set, so an earlier
222    * {@code public, max-age=...} cannot survive alongside it.  Call it before the first byte of the body is written:
223    * once the response is committed, headers can no longer change.
224    *
225    * @param res The response.  Must not be <jk>null</jk>.
226    */
227   public static void markTokenBearing(HttpServletResponse res) {
228      reqnn("res", res).setHeader("Cache-Control", "private, no-store");
229   }
230
231   @Override /* Filter */
232   public void doFilter(ServletRequest req, ServletResponse res, FilterChain chain) throws IOException, ServletException {
233      if (! (req instanceof HttpServletRequest req2) || ! (res instanceof HttpServletResponse res2)) {
234         chain.doFilter(req, res);  // HTT: a non-HTTP servlet request cannot reach a filter mapped into an HTTP container.
235         return;
236      }
237      var result = boundary.check(req2);
238      if (! result.isAllowed()) {
239         reject(res2, result);
240         return;
241      }
242      if (mintsSessionFor(req2))
243         req2.getSession(true);
244      var tokens = new TokenSupplier(boundary, req2);
245      req2.setAttribute(TOKEN_ATTRIBUTE, tokens.get());
246      req2.setAttribute(TOKEN_SUPPLIER_ATTRIBUTE, tokens);
247      req2.setAttribute(HEADER_ATTRIBUTE, boundary.csrfHeader());
248      chain.doFilter(req, res);
249   }
250
251   /**
252    * Whether an allowed request should get a session before the page answering it embeds a token.
253    *
254    * <p>
255    * Only for a {@link CsrfBoundary} with a {@linkplain CsrfTokens#perSession() session-scoped} strategy and
256    * {@linkplain CsrfBoundary#createSessions() session creation} on, only on a safe request, and only when the request
257    * looks like a page load.  Never on a write: a write must already carry the token of a page that had a session.
258    */
259   private boolean mintsSessionFor(HttpServletRequest req) {
260      if (! (boundary instanceof CsrfBoundary b) || ! b.createSessions() || ! (b.tokens() instanceof CsrfTokens.PerSession))
261         return false;
262      if (! MethodSafety.isSafe(MethodSafety.effectiveMethod(req.getMethod(), req.getQueryString(), req::getHeader)))
263         return false;
264      return looksLikePageLoad(req);
265   }
266
267   /**
268    * Whether a request looks like a browser loading a page, as opposed to a script's fetch or a command-line client.
269    *
270    * <p>
271    * With fetch metadata, only a navigation or a {@code document}/{@code iframe} destination counts.  Without it, an
272    * {@code Accept} header naming {@code text/html} does, so {@code curl -H 'Accept: text/html'} also counts, while
273    * {@code Accept: *}{@code /*} never does.
274    */
275   private static boolean looksLikePageLoad(HttpServletRequest req) {
276      var mode = req.getHeader("Sec-Fetch-Mode");
277      var dest = req.getHeader("Sec-Fetch-Dest");
278      if ("navigate".equalsIgnoreCase(trim(mode)) || "document".equalsIgnoreCase(trim(dest)) || "iframe".equalsIgnoreCase(trim(dest)))
279         return true;
280      if (mode != null || dest != null || req.getHeader("Sec-Fetch-Site") != null)
281         return false;
282      var accept = req.getHeader("Accept");
283      if (accept == null)
284         return false;
285      for (var range : accept.split(",")) {
286         var semi = range.indexOf(';');
287         if ("text/html".equalsIgnoreCase((semi < 0 ? range : range.substring(0, semi)).trim()))
288            return true;
289      }
290      return false;
291   }
292
293   private static String trim(String s) {
294      return s == null ? null : s.trim();
295   }
296
297   /**
298    * Answers a rejected request directly, without invoking the chain, so it never reaches application code.
299    *
300    * <p>
301    * The refusal is marked {@code no-store} so neither a browser nor an intermediate cache replays it once the cause
302    * has been fixed.
303    *
304    * <p>
305    * The request body is never read, so the connection is marked {@code Connection: close}.  Without it, a client that has
306    * not yet finished sending the body reuses the connection while the container is closing it, and the next request
307    * on it fails with an empty response.
308    *
309    * <p>
310    * The stream is written to but deliberately not closed: it belongs to the container, which commits and
311    * releases it once the filter returns.  Closing it here would commit the response early and cut off any
312    * outer filter that wraps it.
313    */
314   @SuppressWarnings({
315      "resource" // getOutputStream() returns the container-owned response stream; the filter is not its owner and must not close it.
316   })
317   private static void reject(HttpServletResponse res, BoundaryResult result) throws IOException {
318      res.reset();
319      res.setStatus(result.status());
320      res.setHeader(REJECTION_HEADER, result.reason().name());
321      res.setHeader("Cache-Control", "no-store");
322      res.setHeader("Connection", "close");
323      res.setContentType("application/json;charset=utf-8");
324      var body = "{\"reason\":\"" + result.reason().name() + "\",\"message\":\"" + escape(result.message()) + "\"}";
325      var bytes = body.getBytes(StandardCharsets.UTF_8);
326      res.setContentLength(bytes.length);
327      res.getOutputStream().write(bytes);
328   }
329
330   /**
331    * Escapes a rejection message for a JSON string literal.
332    *
333    * <p>
334    * Written out rather than delegated to a serializer so the rejection path has no dependency on marshalling
335    * configuration: this response must be producible even when the application's serializers are misconfigured,
336    * because a boundary refusal that fails to render degrades into an opaque 500.
337    */
338   private static String escape(String s) {
339      var sb = new StringBuilder(s.length() + 16);
340      for (var i = 0; i < s.length(); i++) {
341         var c = s.charAt(i);
342         switch (c) {
343            case '"' -> sb.append("\\\"");
344            case '\\' -> sb.append("\\\\");
345            case '\n' -> sb.append("\\n");
346            case '\r' -> sb.append("\\r");
347            case '\t' -> sb.append("\\t");
348            default -> {
349               if (c < 0x20)
350                  sb.append(f("\\u%04x", (int)c));
351               else
352                  sb.append(c);
353            }
354         }
355      }
356      return sb.toString();
357   }
358}
